key_insight: Combining machine learning-based nitrogen planning with grower-informed, in-season AI adaptation can reduce fertiliser use while maintaining winter wheat yield and grain quality.
engineering_relevance: Deployable agricultural AI must adapt recommendations to weather, machinery availability and budgets rather than optimise nitrogen rates in isolation.
method: Generate baseline fertilisation plans from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve.
Use a large language model to adapt plans during the season.
Incorporate grower input and operational constraints to keep recommendations executable.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used long-term experiments, replicated field trials and farm deployments; baseline plans matched standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, while adapted plans also retained grain quality standards.
watch_item: Evidence is specific to winter wheat in England; transfer to other crops and regions requires validation.
paper_title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
